subject: Reserved pool: GPU tiering & TPS follow-up
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Subject: Reserved pool: GPU tiering & TPS follow-up

Hi Olivia / Chris —

Thanks again for the call this morning — really helpful to see Quantiv's expected traffic profile. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size a Dedicated (reserved) pool that meets latency and cost targets.

Recap from the call:
- Preferred deploy mode: Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) with VPC peering into your AWS account for data isolation.
- Sustained traffic: ~40 TPS (avg) across inference flows; expected peak bursts up to ~120 TPS for 10-15 minute windows.
- Token mix (rough avg per request): ~75% short (<32 tokens), ~20% mid (32–512 tokens), ~5% long (>512 tokens). Average tokens/request ~480 (estimate).
- Workload mix: primarily text generation (75–80%), embeddings and reranking ~20%, occasional long-form summaries.
- SLO: p95 latency target for generation under 250ms for short prompts; long prompts acceptable up to 2s.
- Security/Compliance: SOC2 required; customer-managed keys ok; VPC peering preferred over full Private on-prem for now.

A few clarifying asks (fast answers will let us produce a targeted sizing recommendation):
1) For the long-tail requests (>512 tokens), are those mostly async batch jobs or latency-sensitive interactive?
2) Do you expect sustained daily throughput to vary by region, or is the 40 TPS estimate global?
3) Any hard constraints on acceptable tail latency for embeddings?
4) Procurement timeline / target start date for reserved capacity (Q1 2027, Q2 2027, etc.)

I attached the demand_profile_v2.csv we sketched during the call — please correct any numbers inline.

Next steps I propose:
- Diego to propose GPU tiering and a 2 sizing options (cost-optimized vs headroom).
- Sync (30 min) with your infra lead to confirm VPC peering + KMS requirements.
- Draft an initial quote and timeline once sizing is agreed.

Available times for a technical sizing follow-up this week: Tue 11/31 10:00–12:00 PT, Wed 12/1 14:00–16:00 PT. If those don't work tell me a couple slots and I’ll coordinate.

Best,
Evelyn

Evelyn — thanks for the crisp recap. A few quick clarifications inline and answers to your asks.

> For the long-tail requests (>512 tokens), are those mostly async batch jobs or latency-sensitive interactive?
Most are async batch (ML pipeline nightly jobs) — roughly 90% async, 10% interactive (user-triggered diagnostics). For interactive long-form we can accept slightly higher latency.

> Do you expect sustained daily throughput to vary by region, or is the 40 TPS estimate global?
40 TPS is global average. We'll have heavier traffic from NA but expect some EU traffic during our business hours. We plan to start in us-west and add eu-west next quarter.

> Any hard constraints on acceptable tail latency for embeddings?
Embeddings can tolerate up to 500ms p95. Generation is the priority.

> Procurement timeline / target start date for reserved capacity (Q1 2027)
Target: early Q1 2027 (Feb rollout ideal). We have an internal approval gate in mid-Jan.

Attached updated numbers — I corrected the long-tail share to 3% (not 5%). We can discuss GPU tiers on the sizing call; our infra team generally prefers to avoid H100 unless we need extreme fp16 perf because our cost model favors A100-class or lower.

Happy to take the sizing call on Wed 12/1 14:00 PT.

—Olivia
Olivia Grant

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Reserved pool: GPU tiering & TPS follow-up (technical notes)

Evelyn / team — jumping in with a tailored technical recommendation based on Olivia's clarified numbers (40 TPS sustained global, 120 TPS peak, avg ~480 tokens, long-tail 3% async). Attached: gpu_tiering_recommendation.pdf (detailed ops notes + cost delta).

High-level sizing options (assumptions: model is a 30B gen model, KV caching for short-prefix reuse, continuous batching enabled):
Option A — Cost-optimized (fits budget, modest headroom):
- 4 x A30 (or equivalent L4 for lower precision models) in a reserved pool.
- Expected sustained throughput ~35–50 TPS for the mixed workload with intelligent batching and prefix cache.
- Peak handling: autoscale to 1 extra node (burst) or leverage lightweight fallback to host models for embeddings to avoid saturation.
- Pros: lower monthly cost; Cons: limited concurrency headroom at 120 TPS peak unless autoscale fast.

Option B — Performance-first (preferred if you want comfortable headroom & single-region resilience):
- 2 x H100 80GB (or 3 x A100 80GB) as the baseline reserved pool.
- Expected sustained throughput ~70–90 TPS with typical batching; can absorb 120 TPS short bursts without immediate autoscale.
- Better for latency-sensitive interactive long prompts and heavy KV cache hits.
- Pros: lower p95, better headroom; Cons: higher cost.

Technical notes / config knobs:
- Batching target: dynamic batching with 50–100ms window for short prompts; reduces cost per token while retaining sub-250ms p95 for short prompts.
- KV cache: enable prefix-level KV caching for chat-like flows — will shift effective throughput by reducing repeated token work.
- Concurrency: aim for 8–12 concurrent streams per GPU for generation-heavy workloads (depends on model quantization).
- Quantization: if you are willing to run an int8 or bf16 profile, A100/A30 can give good perf; H100 best if you need bf16/fp8 speedups.
- Fallbacks: configure automatic fallback to a cheaper variant for embeddings when GPU utilization >85% to preserve latency for generation.

Recommendation: since Quantiv prefers to avoid H100 if possible, propose we size Option B with 3 x A100 80GB as the baseline for Q1 (good balance of perf/cost). We'll include an autoscale policy for burst capacity and a short-term commit that lets you upgrade to H100 if model changes require.

I'll be on the Wed 12/1 14:00 PT call — I can walk through the PDF and run quick simulated throughput numbers.

Diego
